column1: # The arm64 object check's files that state no words of their own the object verdict judges whole (judge-rest, the user's goal of
# 2026-11-20: the object check judged by the test's own words wherever it states them): CORPUS/NAME<TAB>JUDGE<TAB>REASON, JUDGE
#   roundtrip  judged by its own round trip (judge-rest's second round: bin/repr-asm --arch arm64 object-roundtrip, arbace.asm.arm64.objrt:
#              the file assembled by Arbace and linked alone with a stub for its undefined symbols, every instruction of its source,
#              lowered by a64i, equal to the image's word there decoded by a64i, the image otherwise the eval layout's), an own verdict
#   record     judged against llvm-mc 23.1.5's recorded object (test/asm/records/obj-*-llvm-mc-23.1.5.edn), byte for byte
# REASON: why it has no words of its own. Every other file of the object check's corpora (bin/repr-asm --arch arm64 object-check:
# a64-musl, a64-synthetic, mc-aarch64-obj) is judged by its own words, arbace.asm.arm64.objcheck's own-rows: its object runs' CHECK
# lines (piped, or written to %t and read by a viewer on a later RUN line), its -show-encoding runs' stated encodings and its
# disassembly's stated texts (encoded by Arbace) held to Arbace's object, every one met. Every file against the record, byte for
# byte, is the oracle tier's (object-check --oracle, asm-arm64-object-oracle). A file listed here that its own words judge whole is
# stale, one not listed whose words are not judged whole is refused (:not-own): bin/repr-asm --arch arm64 object-check fails on
# either. A record entry whose expected object nothing defines leaves the judge's cases (test/asm/object-out-arm64.edn).
